documents.summary: University IT page telling instructors to write their own AI syllabus statement, because the integrity policy has no AI clause. It supplies five sample statements ranging from a full ban to general permission with attribution.
documents.stance_why: The page says the integrity policy has no separate clause on AI and that "instructors should ... add a statement to syllabi", then offers five templates from a ban to general permission, so the university sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors with tiers.

units.why: The page says the integrity policy has 'do not include a separate clause on the use of AI tools'; a fact about the university framework with no matching type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: policies on academic integrity do not include a separate clause
units.policy: The University's academic integrity policies do not include a separate clause on the use of AI tools.
units.uncovered_note: States that the university's academic-integrity policy has no AI-specific clause, which is why the decision falls to instructors. / States that the university integrity policy has no AI-specific clause.
units.resolution_why: Coder A left policy null (anchor only) and B wrote a normalized statement; the source sentence supports B's wording, which stays within what the passage says. All other codes agree.

units.why: 'instructors should consider how AI can be integrated' hands the decision to instructors, P04; the syllabus-statement duty is a separate unit.
units.anchor: instructors should consider how AI can be integrated into courses
units.policy: Instructors should consider how AI can be integrated into courses.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. Source: 'instructors should consider how AI can be integrated into courses', a recommendation to instructors. Real policy statement; kept as P04 (the decision on AI integration is the instructor's).

units.why: 'add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI' is a syllabus-statement duty, so P09 (should, not must).
units.anchor: add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI
units.policy: Instructors should add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI within courses.
units.resolution_why: Coder A put the syllabus-statement advice in before-course, B in course-start. The passage asks instructors to 'add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI', which is communicating expectations to students, so course-start (B). Type P09 and should agree.

units.why: The bullet 'Alignment with learning goals' lists a consideration for course policy; it ties AI decisions to learning objectives, so P83.
units.anchor: Alignment with learning goals
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account alignment with learning goals.

units.why: 'Equity and access for all students' is a listed consideration for course policy; matches P51.
units.anchor: Equity and access for all students
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account equity and access for all students.

units.why: 'Information security and data privacy' is a listed consideration; P50 protects data.
units.anchor: Information security and data privacy
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account information security and data privacy.

units.why: 'Copyright and academic integrity' is a listed consideration; copyright fits P52 and integrity is only named.
units.anchor: Copyright and academic integrity
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account copyright and academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Also names academic integrity, which P52 does not capture. / Also names academic integrity, which P52 does not cover.

units.why: Names the working group from which the sample statements were adapted, describing how the guidance was produced; P84 covers provenance of policy text.
units.anchor: adapted from the Teachers College AI and Pedagogy Working Group
units.policy: The example statements are adapted from the Teachers College AI and Pedagogy Working Group.

units.why: The page offers five sample statements "reflect[ing] varied stances" that instructors may revise; this is a template menu of tiers of AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: reflect varied stances on using AI in courses and can be revised as needed
units.policy: The five example statements reflect varied stances on using AI in courses and can be revised as needed.

units.why: Example 1 says 'Students are prohibited from using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework', a blanket ban, so P01.
units.anchor: Students are prohibited from using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework or assignments
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase course-start, B during-work. The sentence bans AI use 'to complete coursework or assignments', a rule on the work itself, so during-work. Modality must-not, P01 and prohibit agree.

units.why: The passage states what happens on violation of the no-AI rule: 'Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty'. It is addressed to students at the point of misuse, a binding consequence, so when-misuse and must; it is a sanction, not a stance on AI use, so neutral. P36 treats unauthorized AI use as misconduct.
units.anchor: Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Violation of the no-AI policy is academic dishonesty, handled under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A must, B informs) and unit_stance. The sentence states a binding consequence ("will be considered academic dishonesty") rather than a fact or rationale, so modality is must; it sets no position on whether AI may be used, so unit_stance is neutral. Phase when-misuse and P36 agree.

units.why: Example 1 text on Disability Support Services: 'If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with me'; accommodation, P51.
units.anchor: If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with
units.policy: Students registered with DSS who have an AI accommodation should speak with the instructor directly about their needs.
units.fit_note: Mentions an AI accommodation specifically for DSS-registered students, which P51 only partly covers.

units.why: The sentence says 'Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and how it should be utilized', a commitment by the instructor to state the AI rule for every assignment. That is communicating expectations (course-start) and a binding commitment (must). It lets the assignment set the rule, so P04; the example is the permitting tier.
units.anchor: Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and how it should be utilized
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A course-start, B during-work) and modality (A informs, B must). 'will specify' commits the instructor, so must; the specification tells students the rule before the work, so course-start. P04 and permit agree.

units.why: Example 2: 'Students are responsible for carefully reading and following these guidelines' is a duty to learn the rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for carefully reading and following these guidelines
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase during-work, B course-start. 'Students are responsible for carefully reading and following these guidelines' tells students to learn the course's AI rules, which is the expectations stage, so course-start. P78, must and neutral agree.

units.why: Example 2: 'Proper citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used must be included' names tool and model, so P25 over P24.
units.anchor: Proper citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used must be included
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A require, B permit). 'Proper citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used must be included' is a condition on permitted AI use ('AI Use Permitted for Individual Assignments'); 'require' would mean AI use itself is required. Final permit. Other codes agree.

units.why: The passage says 'Unauthorized use of AI tools will be considered academic dishonesty', the consequence for use outside the assignment's AI rule, addressed to students. It is a binding sanction (must) with no stance on AI use itself (neutral), and P36 is the misconduct type.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of AI tools will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Unauthorized use of AI tools is academic dishonesty, handled under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A must, B informs) and unit_stance. The sentence states a binding consequence ("will be considered academic dishonesty") rather than a fact or rationale, so modality is must; it sets no position on whether AI may be used, so unit_stance is neutral. Phase when-misuse and P36 agree.

units.why: Example 3 lists allowed purposes: 'Helping you find background information about a topic' is search-engine-like understanding, P12.
units.anchor: Helping you find background information about a topic
units.policy: AI tools may be used for helping students find background information about a topic.

units.why: Permitted use: "summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection", AI as a tutor for understanding (P12). P14 (study aids) is close but explanation of material is the core.
units.anchor: Generating summaries or explanations of challenging material
units.policy: AI tools may be used for generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for the student's own reflection.
units.resolution_why: Coder A assigned P12 (tutor for understanding concepts), B P14 (practice, study aids, review). The task is 'generating summaries or explanations of challenging material', which is explanation to understand material, the P12 definition; study aids and review are not mentioned. Final P12.

units.why: Permitted use "Drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts" is writing support (P91).
units.anchor: Drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts
units.policy: AI tools may be used for drafting outlines to help students organize their thoughts.

units.why: Permitted use "Improving grammar and style" is editing support (P91).
units.anchor: Improving grammar and style
units.policy: AI tools may be used for improving grammar and style.

units.why: Under "may NOT be used for any other purposes, including" the example bans drafting writing assignments, i.e. having AI produce submitted text (P19).
units.anchor: Drafting writing assignments
units.policy: AI tools may not be used for drafting writing assignments.

units.why: The same list bans using AI for "Analyzing data". No type captures a ban on AI data analysis (P89 is the permission), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Analyzing data
units.policy: AI tools may not be used for analyzing data.
units.uncovered_note: A specific prohibition on using AI to analyze data (the permitting side is P89, but this rule is a ban, in a course that otherwise lists permitted tasks).

units.why: Example 3: 'permitted only for the specific tasks listed above' is a whitelist default banning everything else; no type covers that exactly, so UNCOVERED rather than P01.
units.anchor: permitted only for the specific tasks listed above
units.uncovered_note: AI use is allowed only for an enumerated list of tasks and nothing else (a closed-list restriction). Coder A fitted this to P05 (name explicit tiers) with a fit note: P05 names categories but not the closed-list restriction.
units.fit_note: A whitelist rule: any use outside the listed tasks is not allowed; P05 covers naming categories but not the closed-list restriction.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: course-start, must, P05 with a fit note; B: during-work, must-not, UNCOVERED. 'permitted only for the specific tasks listed above' is a closed-list restriction on the work, not a naming of tiers, so by the prefer-UNCOVERED rule it stays UNCOVERED; it bars everything off the list, so must-not, and applies to the work, so during-work. unit_stance restrict agrees.

units.why: Example 4: 'Students must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used', P25.
units.anchor: Students must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (Example 4). Source: 'Students must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used.' A real, separate rule from the approval gate (P25). Kept; unit_stance permit because it conditions approved use.

units.why: Requires citation of tool, model and "how they were utilized", which goes beyond tool name to describe use (P25).
units.anchor: citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used and how they were utilized
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A require, B permit). The citation condition attaches to permitted AI use; 'require' would mean AI use itself is required. Final permit. Other codes agree.

units.why: Example 4: 'only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor' is a prior-permission gate; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor
units.uncovered_note: AI use requires explicit prior instructor approval.
units.fit_note: Per-use prior instructor approval; P04 does not capture the approval-before-use gate.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P04 with a fit note; B: UNCOVERED. 'only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor' is a per-use approval gate; P04 (let each instructor or assignment set the rule) does not say that students must get approval before each use. Prefer UNCOVERED over a stretched fit. Other codes agree.

units.why: Example 4: 'must submit a brief written proposal outlining how the AI tool will be used and its purpose' is the approval procedure; UNCOVERED, same gate.
units.anchor: students must submit a brief written proposal outlining how the AI tool will be used
units.uncovered_note: A procedure requiring a written proposal stating how and why AI will be used, submitted before use. / Students submit a written proposal of intended AI use before using it.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A require, B restrict). A written proposal is a precondition for using AI, so restrict, not require. Type UNCOVERED and other codes agree.

units.why: States the criteria instructors use to approve AI proposals: "appropriateness and educational value". Not covered by a type; UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Approval will be granted based on the appropriateness and educational value
units.uncovered_note: Criteria for approving a student's proposed AI use: appropriateness and educational value.
units.fit_note: Sets approval criteria for individual uses rather than course learning objectives.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: UNCOVERED; B: P83 with a fit note. The sentence gives criteria for approving an individual student's proposed use ('appropriateness and educational value'), which P83 (align decisions with learning objectives) only partly covers. It belongs with the approval-gate units, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: The passage says 'Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty and will be addressed according to the policy outlined in this syllabus', the consequence for use without the required approval, addressed to students. A binding sanction (must), no stance on AI use itself (neutral); P36 is the misconduct type.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Unauthorized AI use is academic dishonesty, addressed under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (Example 4). Source confirms the sanction sentence. Coders differed on modality (A must, B informs) and unit_stance. The sentence states a binding consequence ("will be considered academic dishonesty") rather than a fact or rationale, so modality is must; it sets no position on whether AI may be used, so unit_stance is neutral.

units.why: The passage says AI tools 'are generally allowed in this course for research and assignment completion', a default permission for student work, so during-work, may, P02. The attribution proviso is coded as its own unit.
units.anchor: tools are generally allowed in this course for research and assignment completion
units.policy: AI tools are generally allowed in this course for research and assignment completion.
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase course-start, B during-work; B's policy text also folded in the attribution proviso. The rule governs how students do assignments, so during-work. The proviso is a separate rule (coded as its own unit), so the policy text is trimmed to the permission. Type P02, may and permit agree.

units.why: Example 5: 'Students must include citations specifying the exact AI tools and models used', P25.
units.anchor: Students must include citations specifying the exact AI tools and models used
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (Example 5). Source: 'Students must include citations specifying the exact AI tools and models used.' A real rule distinct from the attribution proviso (P25 vs P24). Kept; unit_stance permit because it conditions permitted use.

units.why: The passage says 'Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty', the consequence of non-disclosure, addressed to students. It is a binding sanction (must) and not a stance on AI use (neutral); P28 makes non-disclosure the violation.
units.anchor: Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work is academic dishonesty, addressed under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A must, B informs) and unit_stance. The sentence states a binding consequence ("will be considered academic dishonesty") rather than a fact or rationale, so modality is must; it sets no position on whether AI may be used, so unit_stance is neutral. Phase when-misuse and P28 agree.

units.why: Condition on permission: "all AI-generated content is clearly attributed", a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: all AI-generated content is clearly attributed in the student’s work
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Checked against the source: 'provided that all AI-generated content is clearly attributed in the student's work' is a distinct condition on the general permission (disclose each use, P24), separate from the citation of tools and models. Kept; unit_stance changed from require to permit because it conditions permitted use.
